C.1. HD 10700 (τ Cet)

HD 10700 (τ Cet; HIP 8102; HR 509; GJ 71; TIC 419015728) is a G8V star (Keenan & McNeil 1989) with a debris disk (e.g., Greaves et al. 2004; MacGregor et al. 2016; Sibthorpe et al. 2018) at a distance of d = 3.652±0.002 pc (Gaia Collaboration 2022). Notably, τ Cet has the single highest number of RV observations in our sample (NRV = 1692), yielding the highest sensitivity to HZ planets of the Sun-like stars in the sample. Previously, Tuomi et al. (2013) identified up to five possible planets in this system, of which two (e and f) were also later detected by Feng et al. (2017b). The authors of the latter study used a “differential radial velocity” model that accounted for wavelengthdependent noise in the RV data to identify four planet candidates with Mp sin i < 4 M⊕(RV amplitudes down to 0.3 m s−1) and orbital periods between 20 and 637 days (see Table 8). However, the existence of any planets in this system has been called into question in recent work. Korolik et al. (2023) used long-baseline interferometric data and high-precision spectroscopic observation to measure τ Ceti’s stellar inclination, and found a near-polar orbit. This architecture would mean that the planets reported in Feng et al. (2017b) may not remain dynamically stable, calling into question whether there are planets orbiting this star. We detected a single Keplerian signal with our analysis, which we classified as a FA due to its small amplitude and proximity to the 1/3 annual harmonic. We did not identify any sub-threshold peaks in the RV residuals that correspond to any of the putative planets reported in Feng et al. (2017b). We attribute our non-detection to the more sophisticated treatment of wavelength-dependent noise in previous studies and the disputed nature of these planets.

C.2. HD 33564

HD 33564 (HIP 25110; HR 1686; GJ 196; TIC 142103211) is an F7V star (Gray et al. 2003) at a distance of d = 20.79 ± 0.03 pc (Gaia Collaboration 2022). A single massive (Mp sin i = 9.1 MJ) planet, HD 33564 b, has been reported in this system with an orbital period of 388 days (Galland et al. 2005) using only 15 RV measurements from the ELODIE spectrograph spanning one orbital period. The ELODIE data analyzed by Galland et al. (2005) are not publicly available apart from the points in their Figure 1. To the best of our knowledge, HD 33564 has not been observed by any of the instruments included in this analysis. The limited RV data analyzed in the discovery paper and lack of follow-up observations make HD 33564 b a dubious planet detection.

D. CLASSIFICATIONS OF OTHER SIGNALS DETECTED

Here we comment on systems with other RV signals detected by RVSearch which have not yet been discussed in §5 or Appendices B-C. These systems have no previously-detected planets, so the signals discussed here are either related to stellar activity or instrumental false alarms.

D.1. HD 1581 (ζ Tuc)

HD 1581 (ζ Tuc; HIP 1599; HR 77; GJ 17; TIC 425935521) is an F9.5V (Gray et al. 2006) star at a distance of d = 8.61±0.01 pc (Gaia Collaboration 2022). This star has no known exoplanets, although an observed infrared excess suggests the presence of a circumstellar debris disk (Trilling et al. 2008). We analyzed 550 RV observations of this target from HARPS, CES-LC, CES-VLC, and UCLES spanning a total of 29 years. We found two significant signals at P.01 = 937.0 ± 16.5 d (∼2.6 yr) and P.02 = 15.654 ± 0.006 d. Lovis et al. (2011) predicted a stellar rotation rate for this target of Prot = 16.7 ± 2.6 d, which matches the 15.65-day RV signal we detected. We have therefore designated signal HD 1581.01 as SA-R (indicating rotation-modulated stellar activity). Lovis et al. (2011) also reported a stellar activity cycle for HD 1581 with a period of Pcycle = 1018+51 −47 d, based on 127 log R′ HK measurements from HARPS. This activity period is consistent with our second RV detection (HD 1581.01) within 2σ; therefore, we categorized this signal as being due to stellar activity. This interpretation is supported by a peak in the FWHM GLS periodogram at ≈1000 days.

Both signals are dubious given the multiple clustered peaks in both ∆BIS periodograms and the non-monotonically increasing running-LS periodograms. We note that the putative giant planet in α Cen A (Beichman et al. 2025; Sanghi et al. 2025) has a suggested mass below the RV sensitivity limit, which explains why we did not detect a signal associated with this planet candidate. For α Cen B, we identified one significant long-period signal (LPS) at P ≈12600 days after modeling out the long-term RV trend associated with the stellar binary. This signal is consistent with significant power in the BIS, FWHM, and window function GLS periodograms, but given that the limited RV data cannot sample the full orbit, this signal is likely a systematic.

D.18. HD 185144 (σ Dra)

HD 185144 (Alsafi; σ Dra; HIP 96100; HR 7462; GJ 764; TIC 259237827) is a K0V star (Keenan & McNeil 1989) with no known planets at a distance of d = 5.764 ± 0.002 pc (Gaia Collaboration 2022). Our analysis of this star included 728 RVs from HIRES, Hamilton, and Levy observed over a span of 24 years. We identified three significant RV signals at P.01 = 2338 ± 34 d (∼6.4 yr), P.02 = 363.34 ± 0.69 d, and P.03 = 121.55 ± 0.22 d. The first signal appears as a very strong peak in the S-index GLS periodogram and we observed a strong correlation between the HIRES S-index data and the RVs. Following past studies of this signal that are consistent with our results (Rosenthal et al.

D.19. HD 201091/201092 (61 Cyg A/B)

HD 201091 (61 Cyg A; HIP 104214; HR 8085; GJ 820 A; TIC 165602000) and HD 201092 (61 Cyg B; HIP 104217; HR 8086; GJ 820 B; TIC 165602023) are a well-known binary system consisting of a K5V star (61 Cyg A; Keenan & McNeil 1989) and a K7V star (61 Cyg B; Keenan & McNeil 1989) at distances of dA = 3.4966 ± 0.0007 pc and dB = 3.4964±0.0004 pc (Gaia Collaboration 2022). Neither star hosts any known planets. In the RVs, we see opposite long-term trends for these stars associated with their mutual orbital motions. For 61 Cyg A, we used 300 RVs collected using HIRES, Hamilton, and Levy to identify one significant RV signal at 6918±40 d, which we classified as systematic False Alarm due to a corresponding strong peak in the window function at this period. We note that past analysis of this star also detected an stellar activity cycle with a period of ∼2600 days (Rosenthal et al. 2021; Isaacson et al. 2024), which we see weak evidence for in the GLS periodograms for S-index and H-index. For 61 Cyg B, we analyzed 296 RVs collected using HIRES, Hamilton, and Levy and identified one significant RV signal at 49.012 ± 0.029 d. Past work has attributed this signal to stellar rotation (Rosenthal et al. 2021).

D.20. HD 207129

HD 207129 (HIP 107649; HR 8323; GJ 838; TIC 147407292) is a G0V Fe+0.4 star (Gray et al. 2006) with an imaged debris disk (Krist et al. 2010; L¨ohne et al. 2012) at a distance of d = 15.56 ± 0.01 pc (Gaia Collaboration 2022). The star hosts no known planets. We analyzed 179 RVs from HARPS, CES-LC, and CES-VLC spanning almost 27 years. We found one RV signal at P = 1393 ± 11 d (∼3.8 yr), which is consistent to within 1σ of the literature value for this star’s activity cycle period (P = 1520+171 −139 d; Lovis et al. 2011). Additionally, Laliotis et al. (2023) analyzed this system using RV data from HARPS and UCLES, and found an RV signal at P = 1964 ± 49 d and an S-index signal at P ≈1898 d), which they attributed to a magnetic activity cycle.
